title: Accept D112: records branch athena/records, readers section, open points
summary: Revise the records-history design so the records history is a branch named athena/records, add a readers section and a pre-merge up-to-date requirement, and fill the three open points. Then mark D112 accepted, citing the BRIEF.md addenda of 2026-10-23, and add a CHANGELOG entry. Audience: Sri, who decides, and anyone checking the design.

defaults_applied.how: Prose is written for an outside reader.
The readers section cites the code paths read; unmeasured figures stay labelled reported or estimate.
Only the three named files change.
A verifier checks the diff against the criteria.
Criteria check the reader table content and the stated rules, not just that a section exists.
The design keeps its alternatives and reversal cost.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The addenda in BRIEF.md of 2026-10-23 exist and authorise these decisions; the producer cites them without editing BRIEF.md.
'Cutover after build job 6' matches the existing plan, where job 7 is the cutover; the wording is made explicit.
Reader locations come from the repository's code. The producer greps for reads of records/; the section describes them and no code changes.
Goal: an accepted, internally consistent design that later build jobs follow. Nothing is built.

acceptance_criteria.text: No occurrence of `refs/athena/records` or `refs/athena/*` remains in docs/design/records-history.md or the D112 entry, except where explaining the change from the earlier custom ref. Every place that named the ref (§3 recommendation and assumption, §6.1, §7 table, §10 job 1, §12) now names the branch `athena/records` with its own root. The A4 row says a plain clone carries it.

The design states why a branch: the host's branch rules can forbid force-pushes and deletion, and a plain clone carries it. The host-accepts-`refs/athena/*` assumption and its open point are replaced by the host-rules requirement.

A new readers section lists each reader that reads records/ from the working tree today: status, forecasting and the reference forecaster, scoring, retry carry, audit, introspection, and the study site generator. For each it gives where it reads now (a code path found in the repository) and how it reads after the cutover, for example a worktree of athena/records at a fixed path. It names the build-plan job that moves it. The build plan in §10 is updated so some job owns this work.

The design states that the pre-merge status depends on the host requiring branches to be up to date before merging, so the squash's parent equals the head's base. The text names what happens if the host does not require it.

Open points are filled: pending window 15 minutes (§5.2 states it as the value, not an example), cutover after build job 6, and two weeks between job 7 and job 8. §10 and §12 are consistent with these; §4 and §12 no longer leave these points open.

The design's Status line and D112 in docs/decisions.md say accepted, citing the BRIEF.md addenda of 2026-10-23. D112's Decision, Tradeoff and Provenance text uses the branch name and no longer says 'proposed' or 'not accepted'.

CHANGELOG.md has an entry recording the acceptance and the three changes. The existing entry that says 'Awaiting Sri's decision' is updated or superseded. git diff shows changes only in docs/design/records-history.md, docs/decisions.md and CHANGELOG.md.
Run `git status` and `git diff --stat`: only those three paths changed. Run `cargo test` and confirm it passes, in case a test validates decisions.md format.

out_of_scope: Any code change, including moving the readers
Creating the athena/records branch or configuring host branch rules
Changes to BRIEF.md, athena.toml, or other decisions
departures: The readers section requires finding every reader of records/ in the code, so cost and the chance of a missed reader are somewhat above the reference.
